items.title: NASA Science
items.summary: What creates the colors in Jupiter's clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium, elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops. Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research, although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate. What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image -- and many similar images -- is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter. Juno continues in its looping elliptical orbit, swooping near the huge planet every 33 days and exploring a slightly different sector each time around.Tomorrow's picture: emerging darkness

items.title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD), a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a regularized approximation of local training geometry, producing scalable influence-based values for the policy. items.title: Time Series Structure Learning with Local Causal Parent Discovery
items.summary: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. These challenges complicate the practical application of causal discovery algorithms, which already suffer from high computational and sample complexity in the general case. To mitigate these issues, this work introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD): a sound and complete constraint-based procedure for causal structure learning on multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity. ITPD takes a local-to-global learning approach that discovers the global graph by sequentially discovering the parent set for each variable. ITPD exploits temporal structural priors, graph partitioning, and the local Markov condition to swap higher-order conditional independence tests for lower-order alternatives.

items.summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. items.title: Lang-SVG: Hierarchical Image Vectorization with Language Priors
items.summary: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. However, most existing vectorization methods optimize for pixel-level render- ing fidelity, often producing SVGs that lack alignment with human-perceived object-part hierarchies, making them difficult to manipulate. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. Lang-SVG incorporates granularity-controllable and open-vocabulary segmentation priors to initialize object-part hierarchies and leverages multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with SVG tree context to assign semantic labels to unlabeled nodes. To reduce redundancy, we introduce depth-adaptive simplification to reduce shape complexity and Tree-Guided Pruning
